references.text: The Lord promises to give rain at the right time and bless the land's harvest, a recurring theme of God's blessing through rain and fertility.
A promise that God will give rain at the right time, both autumn and spring rain, so that the people may gather grain, wine, and oil.
Solomon's prayer that God would open the heavens and send rain when the people turn back to Him, linked to the theme of heaven as God's treasury.
God asks Job if he has seen the storehouses for snow and hail, pointing to heaven as God's treasury.
The Lord brings clouds from the ends of the earth, makes lightning for the rain, and sends wind out from His storehouses.
The Lord sends wind out from His storehouses, parallel to the idea of heaven as God's treasury.
A promise that God will open the floodgates of heaven and pour out blessing in abundance when the people bring their tithes to the storehouse.
Jesus teaches about storing up treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, contrasting with earthly treasures.
Paul speaks of the depths of God's riches and wisdom, connecting to God's inexhaustible treasury of blessings.
